stem: During a prescriber call, a never-filled Demerol prescription is brought to a Massachusetts pharmacy 35 days after issue. What is the result?

choices.text: Dispense after confirming that the prescriber still wants the medication supplied.
The Schedule II prescription is invalid because more than 30 days have elapsed since issue.
Use the federal six-month refill clock because Demerol is controlled.
Transfer the prescription before dispensing to restore validity.
Treat 35 days as acceptable when no prior quantity was dispensed.

By contrast, 'Dispense after confirming that the prescriber still wants the medication supplied.' would require that prescriber confirmation could extend an expired Schedule II prescription without a new prescription. The decisive cue appears in 'During a prescriber call, a never-filled Demerol prescription is brought to a Massachusetts pharmacy 35 days after issue. What is the result?'.

related_facts: meperidine (Demerol) is used for pain severe enough to require an opioid when alternatives are inadequate; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.
A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after its issue date.
